title: Queen's Gambit
intro: 1.d4 d5 2.c4: White offers a pawn to pull Black's d-pawn out of the centre. A solid, strategic choice for White.

lessons.title: The Queen's Gambit Declined
lessons.summary: Pressure d5, pin the knight, and avoid the Elephant Trap.

steps.text: The Queen's Gambit starts 1.d4 d5 2.c4. The c-pawn attacks d5 and tempts Black to give up the centre.

steps.hint: Queen's pawn two squares, then the c-pawn two squares.
steps.ifWrong: The Queen's Gambit goes d4, then c4.

steps.text: If Black takes on c4 (the Queen's Gambit Accepted), White takes the centre with e4 and usually wins the pawn back. More often Black declines with 2...e6, holding d5.
Develop your queen's knight and add pressure on d5.
steps.ifWrong: The main line brings the knight to c3, hitting d5.

feedback.g1f3: A good move too. The main line plays Nc3 first, adding pressure on d5.

steps.text: Pin the knight with your bishop: it defends d5, and now it cannot move without losing the queen.
steps.hint: Your dark-squared bishop can reach g5.
steps.ifWrong: The classic move is Bg5, pinning the knight to the queen.
steps.ifRight: The pin adds more pressure on d5.

steps.text: Careful! After 4...Nbd7 5.cxd5 exd5, the pawn on d5 looks free. It is a trap.
Do not fall for the Elephant Trap. Play a safe, solid move instead of taking d5.
steps.hint: Support your centre, develop the king's knight, or bring a rook to the c-file.
steps.ifWrong: Keep it simple: develop and protect your centre.

feedback.c3d5: That is the Elephant Trap: 6...Nxd5! 7.Bxd8 Bb4+ 8.Qd2 Bxd2+ 9.Kxd2 Kxd8 and Black has won a piece.

steps.text: Here Black accepted the gambit with 2...dxc4. Take the centre or get ready to win the pawn back.
steps.hint: A central pawn move, or develop the king's knight.
steps.ifWrong: Use the time to build your centre or develop.
steps.ifRight: Good: the pawn on c4 will not run away.
